findings.title: Google credential key is saved as the zod SafeParse wrapper, which breaks every Google Calendar credential after its first refresh
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), not the parsed token (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:29). Line 97 assigns that wrapper to `key` and writes it to the credential at line 100. This happens even when credential sharing is off. The next time a `GoogleCalendarService` is built, `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` at line 75 gets `{ success: true, data: {...} }` and throws, so the calendar stops working for every user whose token gets refreshed. Fix: use `parseRefreshTokenResponse(...).data` when you write the key.

findings.title: `prisma` is used but never imported, so the Salesforce client throws in production
findings.body: This file never imports `prisma` (grep finds only line 96). It type-checks only because `globalThis.prisma` is declared globally. `packages/prisma/index.ts:58-60` assigns `globalThis.prisma` only when `NODE_ENV !== "production"`. In production, `getClient` therefore throws `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined` on every construction, and every Salesforce operation fails. Add `import prisma from "@calcom/prisma";`.

findings.title: Salesforce refreshes its token on every client creation, skips the sync endpoint, and keeps the stale access token
findings.body: `getClient` now POSTs to Salesforce's token endpoint every time a service is constructed. It does not check expiry first, and it does not go through `refreshOAuthTokens`, so self-hosters with sync enabled still hit Salesforce directly with their own consumer secret. The new token is stored (line 98), but the `jsforce.Connection` is still built with the old `credentialKey.access_token` and `instance_url` (lines 105-106), so the refresh has no effect on the connection that is returned. Also, if the refresh fails, construction now fails (line 86), where before jsforce refreshed lazily. Suggested fix: send the call through `refreshOAuthTokens` and build the connection from `accessTokenParsed.data`.

findings.title: In sync mode the helper returns a raw fetch `Response`, but several callers expect an SDK or axios result
findings.body:
With sync enabled, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns the `fetch` Response object. The fetch-based callers (Lark, Office365, Webex, Zoom) run it through `handleErrorsJson` and similar handlers, so they work. The other callers do not:
- Google reads `res?.data` (googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94), which is undefined on a Response, so `token.access_token` throws.
- HubSpot treats the Response as a `HubspotToken` and writes it as the credential key (hubspot/lib/CalendarService.ts:192-198).
- Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read `tokenInfo.data.error` (zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts:96, and the zohocrm equivalent), which is undefined.

In short, the feature this PR adds is broken for those four apps. The helper also never checks `response.ok`. Fix: have the helper return parsed JSON in a shape callers can rely on, or adapt each caller.

findings.title: The minimum token schema's computed keys both become "[object Object]", so the schema strips expiry fields
findings.body: `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` both evaluate to the literal key `"[object Object]"`. The second overwrites the first, so the schema is `{ access_token: string, "[object Object]"?: unknown }`. `z.object` strips unknown keys, so in sync mode `expires_in`, `expiry_date` and every other field is dropped. For example, Zoom then computes `Date.now() + undefined * 1000 = NaN` as `expiry_date` (zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:122) and stores the placeholder `"refresh_token"` as its refresh token (line 120). Use `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` instead, and validate an expiry field explicitly.

findings.title: The placeholder `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` can overwrite a real refresh token
findings.body: When a refresh response has no `refresh_token`, the helper inserts the string literal "refresh_token". It does this in non-sync mode too. Office365 spreads `tokenResponse.data` over the stored credentials (office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:264), and Zoom assigns `newTokens.refresh_token` (zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts:120). In both cases, a provider response without a refresh token replaces the real stored token with the placeholder. The next refresh then fails, and nothing tells the user why. Leave the field undefined, and let callers keep the existing refresh token.

findings.title: Zoho Bigin sends the credential id as the Cal.com user id
findings.body: `refreshAccessToken(credentialId, credentialKey)` passes `credentialId` as the `userId` argument of `refreshOAuthTokens`. The sync endpoint therefore receives `calcomUserId=<credential id>`, and with it the wrong user's tokens or none at all. The user-only check (`&& userId`) is also bypassed for team credentials. Pass the credential's `userId` instead.

findings.title: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by directory name but the lookup uses the app slug
findings.body: `appStoreMetadata` is keyed by app directory (apps.metadata.generated.ts:98 `googlecalendar`, :146 `zoomvideo`), but `app.slug` is the slug (`google-calendar`, `zoom`, `lark-calendar`; see googlecalendar/_metadata.ts:17, zoomvideo/_metadata.ts:16). For every app whose slug differs from its directory name, including Google Calendar and Zoom, the webhook returns 404 "App not found". Look the app up by `dirName` (select it from `prisma.app`), or search the metadata values by `slug`.

findings.title: Zoom sends `appSlug: "zoomvideo"`, but the app's slug is "zoom"
findings.body: The other callers send the slug (`google-calendar`, `lark-calendar`, `msteams`), but Zoom sends its directory name, while `zoomvideo/_metadata.ts:16` declares `slug: "zoom"`. The parent application's sync endpoint and the webhook's `appSlug` therefore use different identifiers for Zoom.

findings.title: Webhook secret check is not constant-time, and malformed input returns a 500
findings.body: The secret is compared with `!==` instead of `crypto.timingSafeEqual`. If `parse` (line 31) or the decrypt-and-`JSON.parse` step (lines 57-59) throws on a malformed body or wrong key, the error goes unhandled and the endpoint returns 500 instead of 400. Consider `timingSafeEqual` together with `safeParse` and a try/catch around decryption.

findings.title: Sync endpoint request carries no authentication
findings.body: The POST to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` contains only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`. It carries no secret or signature, so the parent application cannot tell that the caller is Cal.com, and anyone who can reach that endpoint can ask it for a user's access token. Consider sending `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET` in a header, the same way the inbound webhook requires it.

findings.title: `tokenResponse.success &&` is dead code now that the helper throws, and the MS error log was removed
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` throws when `success` is false (parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts:21-23), so the `success` guards here, at zoomvideo VideoApiAdapter.ts:108 and at salesforce CalendarService.ts:92 can never be false. The old code logged the zod error and Microsoft's response. The new throw message has neither, which makes Outlook refresh failures harder to diagnose.

contracts.equivalent_path: Previous code: googleCredentialSchema.parse(googleCredentials) stored the parsed object
contracts.before_after: Before, the parsed credential object was stored. After, the SafeParse wrapper is stored, and in sync mode res.data is undefined on a fetch Response
contracts.visible_effect: Google Calendar stops working after the first refresh: the parse at line 75 throws
contracts.failure_mode: Errors other than invalid_grant are swallowed (line 108), so the failure is silent

contracts.action: Inbound webhook upserts a user's credential
contracts.before_after: Looks up appStoreMetadata by slug, but the map is keyed by dirName
contracts.visible_effect: 404 for apps such as google-calendar and zoom
contracts.failure_mode: A thrown parse or decrypt error returns 500

contracts.action: Salesforce getClient refreshes the token on construction
contracts.before_after: There is no expiry check and no sync helper; the stale access token is used afterwards
contracts.visible_effect: In production, every Salesforce call fails with a ReferenceError on prisma
contracts.failure_mode: The client promise rejects, so every CRM operation fails

summary:
This PR should not merge as is: I found two blockers, and the new credential-sync path is broken for several apps. I reviewed all 40 files in this part by reading the code only, without building or running anything.

**Blockers**
- **Google Calendar breaks for everyone, with or without sync:** the refresh code stores the zod wrapper (`{ success, data }`) as the credential key. The next time the service loads, `googleCredentialSchema.parse` throws, so Google Calendar stops working for every user whose token gets refreshed.
- **Salesforce fails in production:** `salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts` uses `prisma` without importing it. The global copy exists only outside production, so every Salesforce client creation throws a `ReferenceError` there.

**Should be fixed in this PR**
- **Raw fetch Response:** in sync mode, `refreshOAuthTokens` returns a raw fetch `Response`, and Google, HubSpot, Zoho Bigin and Zoho CRM read it as an SDK or axios result, so their refresh breaks.
- **Schema strips expiry fields:** in `minimumTokenResponseSchema`, both computed keys evaluate to `"[object Object]"`, so the schema drops `expires_in` and similar fields. Zoom then stores `NaN` as its expiry date.
- **Placeholder refresh token:** the literal string `"refresh_token"` can overwrite a real refresh token for Office365 and Zoom.
- **Wrong user id:** Zoho Bigin sends the credential id to the sync endpoint as `calcomUserId`.
- **Webhook lookup by the wrong key:** the webhook looks up app metadata by slug, but that map is keyed by directory name, so apps such as Google Calendar and Zoom get a 404.
- **Salesforce refresh logic:** it refreshes on every client creation, bypasses the sync endpoint, and builds the connection with the old access token.

**Worth considering**
- **Webhook secret check:** it is not constant-time, and a malformed body returns a 500 instead of a 400.
- **Unauthenticated sync request:** the request to the sync endpoint carries no secret, so the parent application cannot verify that Cal.com is the caller.
- **Zoom slug:** Zoom sends `zoomvideo` where the other apps send their slug (`zoom` here).
- **Dead checks:** some `success` checks can never fail now that the helper throws, and the Outlook error log was removed.
